article.title: Why a Model Can Improve AUC but Make Targeting Worse
article.why: Connect global ranking metrics with the part of the score distribution actually used for campaigns.

paragraphs.en:
A model team may celebrate when AUC rises from 0.78 to 0.81. A higher AUC generally means the model is better at ranking positive cases above negative cases across the full population. That is useful, but a campaign rarely acts on the full population. If only the top five or ten percent of customers can be contacted, improvement in global ranking does not guarantee better targeting where the business actually operates.

Consider two models used to select 100,000 customers from a population of two million. Model B has a higher overall AUC than Model A because it separates medium-risk customers more accurately. However, the ordering among the highest-scoring 100,000 customers may be almost unchanged. In that case, the campaign receives little practical benefit from the AUC improvement.

The situation can be worse. A new model might improve ranking in the middle while slightly damaging ordering at the extreme top. Overall AUC can still increase because it summarizes pairwise ranking performance across many score regions. Yet precision among the customers actually selected for treatment may fall. If contact capacity is fixed, this can reduce conversions even though the headline model metric improved.

This is why evaluation should reflect the decision rule. When the business targets the top x percent, analysts can examine precision@k, recall@k, lift, gain, conversion rate by score band, and the number of true positives captured within the operational cutoff. They should also check stability across time and customer segments.

There is another complication: predictive accuracy is not identical to incremental value. A customer with a high purchase probability may buy without receiving a campaign. A slightly lower-propensity customer may be more persuadable. Therefore, even perfect propensity ranking would not necessarily maximize treatment effect. When randomized experiment data are available, uplift or treatment-effect analysis can provide a closer link to intervention value.

Operational costs also matter. Suppose Model B finds 500 additional likely buyers in the target band but requires expensive data that arrive late. If the campaign loses a day of execution or the feature pipeline frequently fails, the theoretical gain may not survive production.

A better model review therefore asks two questions. First, did the statistical model improve globally? Second, did it improve the decisions the business will actually make? AUC is valuable for broad discrimination, but it should be paired with metrics around the real targeting cutoff, expected economics, temporal stability, and operational reliability. Model improvement is meaningful only when it improves the quality of the action, not merely the number on the evaluation slide.
paragraphs.zh:
AUC 從0.78升到0.81通常代表全體 population 的排序能力改善，但 campaign 往往只觸及 top 5%或10%。若改善只發生在中段，而實際投放的 top band 幾乎沒變，商業價值可能很有限；甚至可能 overall AUC 上升，但 top precision 下降。

因此 evaluation 必須對齊 decision rule，可看 precision@k、recall@k、lift、gain、score band CVR 與 operational cutoff 內抓到的 true positives。同時還要注意 propensity 不等於 incremental effect：高購買機率者可能本來就會買。最後還要把資料延遲、pipeline reliability 與成本納入。真正的 model improvement 應改善實際 action，而不只是 evaluation slide 上的一個數字。
paragraphs.ja:
AUC上昇はpopulation全体でのranking改善を示しますが、campaignが実際に接触するのはtop 5％や10％だけということがあります。改善が中間score帯に集中し、target bandの順序が変わらなければbusiness benefitは小さいままです。場合によってはoverall AUCが上がってもtop precisionが下がります。

そのためdecision ruleに合わせてprecision@k、recall@k、lift、gain、score band別CVRなどを確認します。またpropensityはincremental effectと同じではありません。高確率顧客は施策なしでも購入する可能性があります。さらにdata latencyやpipeline reliabilityも含め、実際のaction qualityが改善したかを評価する必要があります。
